accepted.question_text: For the new asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds constructed by Foscolo, Haskins, and Nordstrom that are cohomogeneity-1 under an SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) action, which of the locally defined G2-instantons near the singular orbit extend to globally defined G2-instantons on the whole manifold X, and, once the global solutions are classified and a nontrivial family is found, what global properties does the resulting moduli space have? In particular, what happens for the D7 family from [FHN18]?

evidence.quote: Recently, infinitely many new examples of AC G2-manifolds X have been found [FHN18]. These examples are cohomogeneity-1 for an action of SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) and so the theory of G2-instantons with these symmetries developed in [LO18] applies. Therefore, the local existence of G2-instantons near the singular orbit in X is guaranteed, and the open question is how many of these local solutions extend globally on X. Once one has classified the global solutions and has a non-trivial family, one can then ask about global properties of the moduli space of solutions, such as those discussed above. This would be specially interesting for the family D7 of [FHN18], as this was not considered in [LO18].

accepted.question_text: Can one construct examples of nearly Kahler instantons on the known nearly Kahler 6-manifolds that occur as links of asymptotic cones of asymptotically conical G2-manifolds - namely S^6, CP^3, S^3 x S^3 (and finite quotients), and the flag manifold F2 - and, for any such nearly Kahler instanton, determine whether it occurs as the limit at infinity of a G2-instanton on an AC G2-manifold and, if it does, how many G2-instantons have that prescribed limit?

evidence.quote: As we have seen, G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds naturally have limits at infinity which are pseudo-Hermitian-Yang-Mills (also known as nearly Kahler instantons) on the nearly Kahler link of the asymptotic cone at infinity. There are very few examples of such connections on nearly Kahler 6-manifolds, and it is an important open problem to try to construct some examples on the known nearly Kahler 6-manifolds which arise as links of asymptotic cones of AC G2-manifolds: that is, S^6, CP^3, S^3 x S^3 (and finite quotients thereof) and the flag F2. Given these examples of nearly Kahler instantons, one can then ask if they arise as limits of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds. If they do arise, it is then natural to ask how many G2-instantons have the given nearly Kahler instanton as their limits at infinity.

accepted.question_text: What is the local deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical G2-manifolds? More specifically, can one understand the local geometry of their moduli space, prove a uniqueness result for the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, decide whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries, and determine the properties of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons, including whether that projection is surjective?

evidence.quote: An obvious problem in this context is to understand the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds; i.e. the deformation theory of such G2-instantons. This is currently being investigated by Joe Driscoll (a PhD student of Derek Harland) and would potentially help solve several interesting questions. For example, can one prove a uniqueness result for the 'basic' G2-instanton on R^7 [GN95] (which has gauge group G2)? Do deformations of G2-instantons with symmetries on AC G2-manifolds also have symmetries? A positive answer to the latter question would mean that we could describe (at least a component) of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds with a cohomogeneity-1 action via the techniques and results described in this survey. There will also be a natural projection map in this context from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons (studied in [CH16]), and so it would be interesting to understand the properties of this map, e.g. whether it is surjective.

accepted.question_text: For the two real 1-parameter families of irreducible G2-instantons described in Theorem 3 on the SU(3)-bundle Q over Lambda^2_-(CP^2), what is the limiting behavior of these G2-instantons as the parameter c tends to +infinity?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3. There are two real 1-parameter families of irreducible G2-instantons on Q parametrized by c >= 0. These are given by ... In particular, the case c = -1 gives flat connections.
What is the limit as c -> +infinity of the G2-instantons in Theorem 3?

accepted.question_text: On the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, Proposition 6 gives a local 1-parameter family of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) that extend smoothly over the singular orbit on the bundle P_id, and Theorem 5 shows that the member with parameter y_0 = 0 extends globally. Do any of the other local instantons from that family, namely those with y_0 != 0, also extend globally, and if they do, is their curvature necessarily unbounded at infinity?

evidence.quote: Proposition 6. Let S^3 be the singular orbit in the Bryant-Salamon R^4 x S^3. There is a one-parameter family of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons, with gauge group SU(2), defined in a neighbourhood of S^3 and smoothly extending over S^3 on Pid.
Theorem 5. The G2-instanton A_lim arising from the case when y0 = 0 in Proposition 6 is given by ... Moreover, A_lim extends as a SU(2)^3-invariant G2-instanton to the Bryant-Salamon R^4 x S^3.

We have seen that the local G2-instanton defined on Pid given by Proposition 6 for y0 = 0 extends globally to the Bryant-Salamon R^4 x S^3 by Theorem 5. A concrete question is whether any of the other local G2-instantons from Proposition 6 for y0 != 0 extend globally or not. Some numerical investigation suggests that if they do, their curvature is unbounded at infinity.

accepted.question_text: Because the natural limits of G2-instantons on asymptotically locally conical (ALC) G2-manifolds are Calabi-Yau monopoles on Calabi-Yau cones, can one develop the theory and produce further examples of Calabi-Yau monopoles on Calabi-Yau cones or on asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-folds that could arise as such limits?
accepted.context_brief: Calabi-Yau monopole limits on ALC ends

evidence.quote: Proposition 9. Let A be a G2-instanton on an ALC G2-manifold (X, phi) ... Suppose there exists a U(1)-invariant connection A_infinity = a + m Phi tensor eta_infinity ... such that ... Then (a, Phi) is a Calabi-Yau monopole on the Calabi-Yau cone (1, +infinity) x Gamma.

Proposition 9 shows that the natural limits of G2-instantons on ALC G2-manifolds (if they exist) are Calabi-Yau monopoles on Calabi-Yau cones. These observations further motivate the study of Calabi-Yau monopoles on cones or AC Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

accepted.question_text: For the many asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds that are close to a degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit and are typically only U(1)-invariant, can one construct G2-instantons that are correspondingly close, in an appropriate sense, to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the limiting cone?

evidence.quote: It has been shown that [FHN17] there are many ALC G2-manifolds which are close to the degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit, and the typical example will only be U(1)-invariant. It is therefore interesting to attempt to construct G2-instantons on these ALC G2-manifolds which are, in a sense, close to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the cone.

accepted.question_text: What is the deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds, how does it relate to the deformation theory of Calabi-Yau monopoles on asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-folds, and what is the image of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons on an ALC G2-manifold to the space of Calabi-Yau monopoles on the asymptotic Calabi-Yau cone?

evidence.quote: As in the AC case, it would be good to have a deformation theory for G2-instantons on ALC G2-manifolds. This would have obvious relations to the deformation theory of Calabi-Yau monopoles on AC Calabi-Yau 3-folds, which also needs to be developed. In particular, one can ask about the image of the projection map from the moduli space of G2-instantons on an ALC G2-manifold to the space of Calabi-Yau monopoles on the Calabi-Yau cone which appears at the end of the ALC G2-manifold.

accepted.question_text: For irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant SU(2) G2-instantons on the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 x S^3 that extend smoothly on the bundle P_1, what happens in the unresolved parameter region 0 < f_1^+ - 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+? In particular, which initial conditions in that region produce globally defined instantons with bounded curvature, which do not, and how should the corresponding existence and non-existence picture be completed for the broader Bogoyavlenskaya family of metrics?

evidence.quote: Theorem 7. ... If f_1^+ <= 1/2, or g_1^+ >= 0 with g_1^+ >= f_1^+, then A extends globally to R^4 x S^3 with bounded curvature if and only if A has gauge group U(1) ... If f_1^+ >= 1/2 + g_1^+ > 1/2, then A is irreducible and extends globally to R^4 x S^3 with bounded curvature.

On the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, we have shown non-existence for irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) and bounded curvature for g_1^+ > 0 and f_1^+ <= 1/2 or g_1^+ >= f_1^+, and existence for f_1^+ >= 1/2 + g_1^+ > 1/2. This currently leaves open the region where 0 < f_1^+ - 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+, which should be investigated so as to describe the full moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1}. Some numerical investigation indicates that some of these initial conditions may lead to globally defined instantons with bounded curvature and some may not. Some of the existence and non-existence results for instantons for the BGGG metric extend, with suitable modifications, to all of the Bogoyavlenskaya metrics, but some do not, so it would be good to address this gap.

accepted.question_text: How do G2-instantons on the Bogoyavlenskaya family of G2-manifolds behave as the underlying metric is deformed by changing the asymptotic circle size? In the large-circle limit, do these instantons converge to G2-instantons for the Bryant-Salamon metric on R^4 x S^3, and in the small-circle limit, what precise relation do they have to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold?

evidence.quote: An interesting problem is to investigate the behaviour of G2-instantons as the underlying metric is deformed. For instance, we have G2-instantons on all of the Bogoyavlenskaya G2-manifolds, and we would want to analyse these instantons as the size of the circle at infinity gets very large or small. When it gets very large we expect them to resemble G2-instantons for the Bryant-Salamon metric in R^4 x S^3. When it gets very small, there may be a relation with Calabi-Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold (as in [Oli16] or problem (b) above).

accepted.question_text: The moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1} of irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on the BGGG manifold is non-compact. Can this moduli space be compactified, and what bubbling behavior occurs as one or both of the parameters f_1^+ and g_1^+ tend to infinity? In particular, does one obtain bubbling phenomena analogous to those proved for the Bryant-Salamon case, possibly related to anti-self-dual instantons on Taub-NUT?

evidence.quote: Theorem 7. The moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1} of irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) on the BGGG metric, smoothly extending on P1, contains a nonempty (and unbounded) open set which is parametrised by U subset R^2.

Even if we can describe the moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1}, it will be non-compact so, just as in the Bryant-Salamon case, we will want to compactify it. It is therefore certainly an interesting problem to investigate the behaviour of the family of instantons from Theorem 7 when one or both of f_1^+ and g_1^+ go to infinity. We would expect bubbling phenomena as in the Bryant-Salamon case in Theorem 6, with possible relationship to the ASD instantons on Taub-NUT found in [EH01].
